description: A single composite schematic (no data plot, micrograph or photograph) illustrating selective laser melting (SLM) of an Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni low-density steel from powder. The large upper panel is a 3D perspective drawing of the machine build area: a grey substrate plate on a lift platform carrying small square printed coupons, a red laser beam descending from a block labelled "Laser", a triangular recoater arm labelled "Powder feed container" with a black arrow marked "Moving direction", and a dark "Overflow container" on the right. Yellow dotted leader lines link the platform to two inset details. The lower-left inset, titled "Scanning strategy", shows two overlapping hatched squares labelled "Layer n" and "Layer n+1" whose hatch (scan) vectors are rotated relative to one another, with an internal angle annotated "67°". The lower-right circular inset is a cross-section of the process zone: an arrow "Laser beam moving direction" above a red beam that creates a "Melt pool" in a grey "Fabricated part" resting on a hatched "Substrate", with loose spherical particles labelled "Fe30Mn9AlC3Ni0.6Cr powder" ahead of the beam. The figure explains powder delivery, melting and interlayer re-scanning; apart from 67° and the composition string, no process parameters or numeric values are printed.

observations.observation: The figure is a schematic (drawing), not a photograph or measurement plot; it renders the SLM machine layout in 3D perspective.
The main panel labels the laser source as 'Laser', the powder-delivery recoater as 'Powder feed container' with an arrow marked 'Moving direction', and the excess-powder bin as 'Overflow container'.

The lower-left inset is titled 'Scanning strategy' and contains two overlapping hatched squares labelled 'Layer n' and 'Layer n+1', whose scan vectors are rotated relative to each other by an annotated angle of 67°.

The lower-right circular inset is a cross-section with the printed labels 'Melt pool', 'Fabricated part', 'Substrate' and the arrow annotation 'Laser beam moving direction', showing the melt pool penetrating into previously fabricated material.
In the cross-section inset the starting powder is drawn as loose spherical particles and is labelled 'Fe30Mn9AlC3Ni0.6Cr powder', i.e. with a 0.6Cr addition in the inset string.
The inset powder label 'Fe30Mn9AlC3Ni0.6Cr powder' differs from the caption's alloy designation 'Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni' (no Cr stated in the caption composition); both readings are reported as printed.
The caption states the figure is a schematic depicting the SLM preparation of an Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni alloy from Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni powder.
The citing text states two sample sizes were printed, 75 × 12 × 12 mm and 10 × 10 × 10 mm, on an SLM Solutions SLM280 printer, with the substrate pre-heated to 200 °C.
The citing text states argon of 99.99% purity was used and the chamber oxygen content was kept below 300 ppm during printing.
The citing text states laser powers of 70, 90, 110, 130 and 150 W were used, corresponding to laser energy densities of 58.33, 75.00, 91.67, 108.33 and 125.00 J/mm³.
The citing text states spot diameter 0.1 mm, layer thickness 0.02 mm, hatch space 0.08 mm and scanning speed 750 mm/s.

The citing text states samples printed at the various laser powers are denoted P-70, P-90, P-110, P-130 and P-150, and that the scanning strategy used overlapping strips with a rotation between adjacent layers to reduce crystallographic texture.

The 67° hatch rotation shown in the 'Scanning strategy' inset is the visual counterpart of the citing statement that adjacent layers are rotated to minimise laser vector coincidence and crystallographic texture.

subfigures.description: 3D schematic of the SLM build platform: lift table with grey substrate plate and several small square printed coupons, a red laser beam from a block labelled 'Laser', a recoater arm labelled 'Powder feed container' with a black arrow labelled 'Moving direction', and a dark 'Overflow container' at right. Yellow dotted lines point to both insets.

Inset titled 'Scanning strategy': two overlapping hatched squares labelled 'Layer n' and 'Layer n+1', their hatch/scan directions rotated with respect to each other; the rotation is annotated '67°' between the two hatch families.

Circular cross-section inset of the melt zone: black arrow 'Laser beam moving direction', red laser beam, 'Melt pool' in a grey 'Fabricated part' on a hatched 'Substrate', and spherical powder particles labelled 'Fe30Mn9AlC3Ni0.6Cr powder' lying ahead of the beam.
